title: Smooth affine schemes lift across arbitrary quotient maps of the base ring
statement: Let $R\twoheadrightarrow R_0$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings. Let $T_0$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] equipped with a smooth morphism $T_0\to\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then there exist an affine scheme $T$, a smooth morphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, and an $R_0$-isomorphism $a:T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}R_0\xrightarrow{\sim}T_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. No nilpotence, locality or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on the base rings. The zero ring and empty affine scheme are allowed.

source.place: Tag 07M8, proposition-lift-smooth, assertion (2), in affine-scheme form: a smooth R_0-algebra A_0 is A/IA for a smooth R-algebra A. The isomorphism is of R_0-algebras.

proof.text: Choose an affine presentation $T_0\cong\operatorname{Spec}B_0$. The affine spectrum correspondence gives an $R_0$-algebra structure on $B_0$ inducing the specified structure morphism. Smoothness is invariant under the chosen affine isomorphism, and the affine smoothness equivalence gives that $R_0\to B_0$ is a smooth ring map. Put $I=\ker(R\to R_0)$, so $R/I\cong R_0$.

source.place: Tag 07M8, proposition-lift-smooth (2), affine translation; Tags 01V6 and 02H6

proof.text: The smooth algebra $B_0$ is finitely presented by the definition of a smooth ring map and flat by the smooth-flat theorem. For every prime $\mathfrak p_0\subset R_0$, smooth base change makes $\kappa(\mathfrak p_0)\otimes_{R_0}B_0$ smooth over the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p_0)$, hence a local complete intersection by the smooth-over-field theorem. Thus $R_0\to B_0$ is syntomic, with precisely the flatness, finite presentation and fibre conditions required by the syntomic lifting theorem.

source.place: Tag 07M8 (2), first sentence; Algebra Tag 00TA, lemma-smooth-syntomic; Tag 00SL, definition-lci

proof.text: Apply the syntomic lifting theorem to $R\twoheadrightarrow R_0$ and $B_0$. Obtain a syntomic $R$-algebra $B$ and an $R_0$-algebra isomorphism $\beta:B/IB\xrightarrow{\sim}B_0$. In particular $B$ is flat and finitely presented over $R$. We will localize $B$ without changing this quotient.

source.place: Tag 07M8 (1) used in the proof of (2)

proof.text: For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ containing $IB$, put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$, so $I\subset\mathfrak p$, and let $\mathfrak p_0\subset R_0=R/I$ be its image. The fields $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak p_0)$ are identified by sending a fraction of classes modulo $\mathfrak p$ to the same fraction modulo $\mathfrak p_0$. The quotient-tensor comparison and $\beta$ give an isomorphism of fibre algebras $$B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong B_0\otimes_{R_0}\kappa(\mathfrak p_0).$$ Explicitly $b\otimes\lambda\mapsto\beta(\bar b)\otimes\lambda$, with inverse obtained by lifting $\beta^{-1}(b_0)$ to $B$; changes of lift lie in $IB$ and tensor to zero. Both maps preserve products on pure tensors. The right side is smooth by smooth base change. Consequently the left side is smooth at the prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ (take localization element $1$). Localized flatness gives $R_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ flat, while finite presentation allows $g=1$ in the pointwise fibre criterion. That criterion proves that $R\to B$ is smooth at every $\mathfrak q\in V(IB)$.

source.place: Tag 07M8 (2), smoothness near V(IB); Algebra Tag 00TF, lemma-flat-fibre-smooth

proof.text: Let $H=H_{B/R}$. Its zero locus is the nonsmooth locus, so the preceding step gives $V(H)\cap V(IB)=\varnothing$. Therefore $V(H+IB)=\varnothing=V(B)$. The zero-locus/radical theorem gives $\sqrt{H+IB}=B$, hence $1\in H+IB$ (a power of $1$ is still $1$). Choose $h\in H$ and $j\in IB$ with $h+j=1$. Thus $h\equiv1\pmod {IB}$, and the singular-ideal localization theorem says that $A=B_h$ is smooth over $R$. This is the required single localization; no finiteness of $I$ or nilpotence is used.

source.place: Tag 07M8 (2), final localization; Smoothing Tag 07C5, definition-singular-ideal; Algebra Tag 00TC, lemma-locally-smooth

proof.text: The map $A=B_h\to B_0$ sending $b/h^n$ to $\beta(\bar b)$ is well defined because the image of $h$ is $1$. It kills $IA$ and gives $\gamma:A/IA\to B_0$. Conversely send $b_0\in B_0$ to the class of $b/1$, for any lift $b\in B$ of $\beta^{-1}(b_0)$; two lifts differ by $IB$, so give the same class. These maps are ring homomorphisms. Their composites fix $B_0$ and the classes of all $b/1$; they also fix $h^{-1}$ because $h=1$ in $A/IA$. Fractions generate $A$, so the maps are inverse. They fix the image of $R_0$, hence $\gamma$ is an $R_0$-algebra isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 07M8 (2), final localization preserves the prescribed quotient

proof.text: Set $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The affine smoothness equivalence shows that $T\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth. The affine fibre-product theorem identifies its base change with $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RR_0)$. The quotient-tensor comparison identifies this algebra with $A/IA$; on pure tensors the map is $a\otimes\bar r\mapsto ra\bmod IA$, so it is multiplicative and respects the $R_0$-structure. Compose with $\gamma$ to obtain an $R_0$-algebra isomorphism $A\otimes_RR_0\cong B_0$. Taking its inverse spectrum morphism and the chosen $\operatorname{Spec}B_0\cong T_0$ gives exactly $a:T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}R_0\cong T_0$ over $R_0$. If $B_0=0$, the prime-indexed arguments are vacuous and the same quotient and localization maps apply; in particular the zero base ring and the empty affine scheme require no exception.

source.place: Tag 07M8 (2), affine-scheme conclusion; Schemes Tags 01I4 and 01JQ
